title: Curated timeseries tiling and oblique-aggregates mart for Console usage
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Goal: build a compact, query-friendly timeseries mart that supports high-cardinality slicing for Console dashboards (cost, latency, usage) without exploding storage or query latency. We will implement a tiling strategy (hour/day/week tiles) combined with pre-computed oblique aggregates (selected multi-dimension rollups) so common cross-filter queries are served from curated tables rather than ad-hoc heavy scans.

Scope and rationale:
- Input: invocation and route event stream (ingestion topic) with fields: event_id, timestamp, workspace_id, route_id, model_variant, region, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, billing_amount_usd, session_id, cache_hit boolean.
- Pain: current ad-hoc joins on raw calls table cause high latency for dashboards and spike query costs for console power users; backfills and rollups take too long for near-real-time needs.
- Approach: produce a tile_aggregates mart (hourly base tile + daily rollups) and an oblique_rollups mart that contains pre-aggregates for common dimension combinations (workspace x route, workspace x model_variant, route x region, workspace x feature_flag). Oblique aggregates are chosen based on query heatmap and cardinality heuristics to cap state growth.

Schema (proposal summary):
- tile_aggregates(hour_tile_start, hour_tile_end, workspace_id, route_id, model_variant, region, requests_count, tokens_sum, cost_sum_usd, median_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, kv_cache_hits, unique_sessions_hll, updated_at)
- daily_rollups(date, workspace_id, route_id, requests_count, tokens_sum, cost_sum_usd, p95_latency_ms)
- oblique_rollups(tile_start, tile_granularity, agg_key_hash, agg_dims, requests_count, tokens_sum, cost_sum_usd, unique_sessions_hll, approx_distinct_models)

Implementation notes and optimizations:
- Use streaming micro-batch (Beam/Spark Structured Streaming) to emit idempotent hourly tiles. Deduplicate by event_id and apply late-arrival watermarking (max 10m).
- Store tiles as Parquet with partitioning by date and workspace_id. Use dictionary encoding and ZSTD compression tuned for our cardinality profiles.
- Represent unique session counts with HyperLogLog sketches in the parquet cell to keep row width small and enable cheap merges.
- Oblique_rollups will use an encoded agg_key_hash to avoid many nullable columns; keep a separate mapping table for decoding during debugging.
- Build sparse storage for oblique combinations: only store combinations observed above a minimum threshold (e.g., 25 events per hour) to limit blowup; materialize cold combos into lower-granularity summaries.
- Add Bloom filter sidecars or partition-level min/max statistics to speed queries that filter by route_id or workspace_id.
- Compaction: hourly delta tiles will be compacted into daily tiles within 24h to reduce small-file overhead. Implement a background compaction job that maintains write amplification < 2x.

Read patterns and SLAs:
- Dashboard short queries: expectation < 2s for top-20 precomputed slices.
- Time series queries spanning many workspaces: served via aggregate helpers that stitch tiles with vectorized aggregation.
- Near-real-time freshness: tiles available within 5 minutes of event time 95% of the time.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end pipeline produces correct hourly tiles for 1 week of historical test data with dedupe and watermarking applied.
- Console cost and latency dashboards show >= 10x lower query cost for representative queries compared to scanning raw calls table.
- Query latency for top 20 slices is < 2s on dev cluster.
- Storage growth for oblique_rollups does not exceed projected budget (estimate: +18% raw storage vs current denorm table for first 6 months).

Risks and open questions:
- Selection strategy for oblique aggregates may miss uncommon but expensive slices — need tooling to detect and auto-promote patterns.
- HLL sketch merging accuracy tradeoffs for small workspaces; we may need a fallback exact count path for audits.
- Cross-team dependency on ingestion watermarking and dedupe correctness (see dependencies).

Deliverables:
- Design doc with schema and tiling heuristics (link in comments).
- Streaming job implementation and tests.
- Compacting/compaction scheduler job.
- Query helpers and documented usage examples for Console front-end engineers.
